title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Ceiling on a Redetermined Dependency Allowance by Age of the Determination
content:
For a dependency redetermination on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, the redetermined dependency allowance is capped according to the age of the latest monetary determination on the claim. That age is the number of calendar days from the latest monetary determination date on the claim to the handling date. The weekly benefit amount against which the ceiling is set is the one on the claim.

## The ceiling

| Age of the latest monetary determination | Ceiling on the redetermined dependency allowance |
|---|---|
| More than 90 days | 0.075 (7.5 percent) of the weekly benefit amount, rounded to the cent |
| More than 21 days but no more than 90 days | 0.08 (8 percent) of the weekly benefit amount, rounded to the cent |
| No more than 21 days | No ceiling |

Where a ceiling applies, the redetermined dependency allowance is the lesser of the allowance computed for the dependents counted and the ceiling. The ceiling is applied to the redetermined allowance before the allowance on the claim is subtracted from it.

## Boundary days

| Age of the determination | Ceiling |
|---|---|
| 21 days | None |
| 22 days | 8 percent |
| 90 days | 8 percent |
| 91 days | 7.5 percent |

### Hypothetical figures

For a weekly benefit amount of 346.00, the 8 percent ceiling is 27.68 and the 7.5 percent ceiling is 25.95. An allowance of 45.00 computed for the dependents counted, on a determination 120 days old, is capped at 25.95; against an allowance on the claim of 15.00 the increase is 10.95.
